newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end slightly higher after late rally.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end slightly higher after late rally.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered from a slump in late trading Tuesday to finish slightly higher.

Traders and analysts said the bolsa crossed into positive territory while the Dow Jones industrial average was extending its gains late in the session, though the Mexican rally was a pale shadow of the surge on Wall Street.
"The market did not respond to the Dow Jones. No one believed in yesterday's late gains, and several key blue chips could not stand the pace," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 6.45 points, or 0.17 percent, at 3,805.10.
"Yesterday's rally was make-believe, and so the market returned to its lateral channel today," said an equity analyst who asked not to be identified.

Traders said an expected rise in Mexican Treasury bill rates later in the day tempered the reaction in the Mexican stock market to strong gains by the Dow industrials, which closed up 135.26 points at 6,587.16.
Dealers said Telmex L shares, which accounted for 17 percent of the 77.95 million shares traded during the session, weighed most on the bourse's last-minute recovery.

The stock ended up 22 centavos (three centavos) at 16.28 pesos ($2.06). Telmex L shares lagged the company's American Depositary Receipts, which climbed 1-1/8 to 41-1/8, as the dollar value of local shares increased in line with a stronger peso.
Traders said a stronger peso also prompted arbitrage trading in Televisa, whose CPO shares fell 90 centavos (11 cents) to 102.10 pesos ($12.97), while the media company's ADRs gained 1/2 to 25-3/4.
Financial group GFB's B shares ended up seven centavos (1 cent) at 2.54 pesos (32 cents) after falling sharply on Monday.
